runs.text: The Bible speaks of the relationship between God the Father and His Son Jesus. Scripture tells us that the Father gives all things to His Son. The Son does nothing except that which He sees His Father do. This Father / Son relationship is the first foundation of the government of God. The Father and Son also share a Spirit.
Most people are surprised to learn that the Bible calls the Father, “
The God of our Lord Jesus Christ.
(See Ephesians 1:17) Jesus has a God. He prayed to his Father just as he directs us to pray. (See Matthew 6:9)
Jesus is divine because He is God’s begotten Son. He received His name as God because of inheritance. “Hebrews 1:4
He hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name
WHO IS GOD?
1. How many Gods did Israel worship?
Deuteronomy 6:4
Hear, O Israel:
The LORD our God is one LORD.
Note:
There is only one God. The Hebrew literally reads: Jehovah our Elohim (God) is one Jehovah. (See Mark 12:29,32,34) (1 Corinthians 8:4)
2. How many Gods did the New Testament Church worship?
Ephesians 4:4
There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; 5 One Lord, one faith, one baptism, 6
One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.
Note:
Not only does it repeatedly say the term “one God," but it says that “God the Father” is “above all.”
3. Did Jesus have a God?
John 20:17
I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.
Note:
Ephesians 1:17 says, “
The God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory.
4. Life eternal is knowing the only true God, and whom?
John 17:3
And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.
1 Timothy 2:5
For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.
Note:
Polytheistic trinitarianism (believing in more than one god) is a belief in “
three co-equal co-eternal beings that make up one God
”. The belief in three co-eternal gods is accepted as a fundamental Christian doctrine. But is the belief in three co-eternal gods found in the Bible?
There are several texts that are used to support the belief in three co-eternal gods, but a closer investigation of these texts will show “One God” and His divine yet subordinate Son.
The Father and Son also share an omnipresent, independent spirit. This omnipresent spirit is not a third god, but is the spirit of God and His Son.
THREE CO-ETERNAL GODS?
5. Didn’t the apostles baptize in the name of three gods?
Matthew 28:19
Go ye therefore, and teach all nations,
baptizing
[immersing]
them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.
Note:

All recorded baptisms in Scripture were done in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. (See Acts 2:38, 8:12, 10:48, 19:5, 22:16, Romans 6:3). Thus, we face two possibilities: either the disciples were disobeying a direct command from Jesus himself, or we have an incorrect understanding of what this verse meant by the word “baptizing”. The words baptism and immersion are often used interchangeably. This verse could be saying: “immersing them in the doctrine of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit”.
Strong’s Concordance states that the word (
baptiszo

when used in the New Testament more often refers to our union and identification with Christ than to our water baptism”. An example is in Mark 16:16: “Christ is saying that a mere intellectual assent is not enough. There must be a union with him, a real change.
” (Bible Study Magazine, James Montgomery Boyce, May 1989)
6. Does the account of Jesus' baptism show three-co-eternal Gods?
Matthew 3:16
And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him,
and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:
And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
Note:
It is certainly difficult to find
three co-eternal beings
in this text. It says Jesus saw the
Spirit of God
, not “God the Holy Spirit”, descending like a dove. The best this verse can do is prove that God has a Son and that they have an independent Spirit.
7. Wouldn’t Jesus’ presence in the beginning mean that He has always been with God?
John 1:1
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
2 The same was in the beginning with God. 3
All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.
Note:
The context in verse 3 shows us that “In the beginning” means the beginning of the creation of the world, not in the beginning of eternity.
Before Jesus was begotten, the Father was without His Son. Jesus was begotten of the Father at a point in time in the distant past. He is God’s actual Son, begotten before the existence of the world.
8. Does John 1:1-3 say that Jesus was God?
John 1:1
In the beginning was the Word, and
the Word was with God, and the Word was God
. 2 The same was in the beginning with God. 3 All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.
Note:
Yes, Jesus is divine, but He still called his father, “My God.” (See John 20:17.) Jesus received divinity from His Father because He was begotten of His Father, by inheritance. (See Hebrews 1:4.)
9. Does the Bible say that Jesus came from everlasting?
Micah 5:2
But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel;
whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.
Note:
It is not apparent in most translations, but in Micah 5:2, the Hebrew word
yowm
(03117) is found just before the word everlasting. Strong’s tells us that
yowm
(03117) means a specific (day). In other words, this text is saying that Jesus was begotten on a specific day. He came from the (days) of everlasting.
The word
yowm
(03117) is the same word found in Genesis 1:5, “evening and morning were the first
yowm
(03117) day.” He was begotten on a specific day in eternity. So, yes, He is from “a day in everlasting”!
BY INHERITANCE JESUS IS DIVINE:
10. How did Jesus obtain His excellent name that deserves worship as divine?
Hebrews 1:4
Being made so much better than the angels, as He hath
by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.
Note
: In Hebrews 1:8 God the Father refers to Jesus as “God”! This proclamation is in the context of Jesus as God’s begotten son.
“Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son.”
Hebrews 1:5
Jesus received all things from his Father by inheritance. By inheritance Jesus obtained His excellent name. Genesis 1:24 tells us that: “
God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind.”
Yes, Jesus is divine because God was His father.
11. How did Jesus obtain a position where all things were under Him?
1 Corinthians 15:27
For he (God) hath
put
all things under his feet

. But when he saith all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him. 28 And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself
be subject unto him
that put all things under him
that God may be all in all
Note:
If Jesus was
co-eternal
then He would always have had all things. This Scripture clearly states that the Son is
subject to the Father who put all things under Him
WAS JESUS GOD’S SON?
12. Has Jesus always existed or was He at some point begotten of His Father?
John 3:16
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son,
that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
Note:

Jesus was not a created being. He was begotten of His Father. He was also sent. (See John 3:17). If God sent His Son, then God had to have had a Son to send. This means that Jesus was begotten prior to His becoming the son of man, and prior to the creation of this world. God really did send His Son!
13. How did Jesus obtain His life and power?
John 5:26
For as the Father hath life in himself; so hath he given to the Son to have life in himself.
Matthew 28:18
And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying,
all power is given unto me
in heaven and in earth.
Colossians 1:19
For it pleased the Father that in him should all fulness dwell.
Note:
So we see that Jesus received all things from His Father. But the doctrine that Jesus is
co-eternal
teaches that Jesus has always had all things and that Jesus did not have a beginning.
The Bible is clear, God sent His real Son! So, to teach the error that
Jesus is eternal
is to teach that Jesus was not begotten, but that He has always existed. It was for this reason that this Father-Son study is included in the “
Forgotten Truth Bible Tracts.
IDENTIFYING THE HOLY SPIRIT:
14. Who is the comforter that the Father would send?
John 14:16
And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter
, that he may abide with you for ever; 17
Even the Spirit of truth
; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you. 18
I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.
Note
: The Father gives us another Comforter. Jesus explains who this Comforter is. “I will not leave you comfortless: “
I will come to you
”… Jesus is our Comforter. (See tract #9, “
The Holy Spirit.
15. Whose Spirit is it? God’s, or Christ’s?
Romans 8:9
Ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if so be that the
Spirit of God
dwell in you. Now if any man have not the
Spirit of Christ,
he is none of his.
Philippians 1:19
For I know that this shall turn to my salvation through your prayer, and the supply
of the Spirit of Jesus Christ
Note:
The Spirit is the Father’s Spirit, shared with His Son.
16. Does the Holy Spirit have an owner?
Genesis 6:3
And the LORD said,
My spirit
shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh.
Note:
Genesis 6:3 shows that the Holy Spirit is God’s Spirit. (See also 2 Corinthians 3:17)
2 Corinthians 3:17
Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord
is, there is liberty.
Isaiah 61:1
The spirit of the Lord God

is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound.
Acts 2:17
And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith God,
I will pour out of my Spirit
upon all flesh.
WHO SHOULD WE WORSHIP?
17. Who do true worshippers worship?
John 4:23
, But the hour cometh, and now is, when the
true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth
for the Father seeketh such to worship him.
Note:
Jesus tells the woman at the well that true worshippers should worship the Father.
18. Did Jesus allow people to worship him also?
John 9:35
Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when he had found him, he said unto him,
Dost thou believe on the Son of God
? 36 He answered and said, Who is he, Lord, that I might believe on him? 37 And Jesus said unto him, Thou hast both seen him, and
it is he that talketh with thee.
And he said, Lord, I believe. And he
worshipped
him.
Note:

Jesus asked the blind man, dost thou believe on the Son of God. There is a link between Jesus being the Son of God and receiving worship. By inheritance Jesus received His identity as God. (Hebrews 1:4) Simply put, Jesus is divine because He is God’s Son.
19. Why did the Apostle Peter worship Jesus?
Matthew 14:32
And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased.
Then they that were in the ship came and
worshipped
him, saying, Of a truth thou art the
Son of God
Note:
Only divine beings are worthy of worship. Jesus deserves worship because He is the Son of God.
20. To whom does confessing that Jesus is Lord bring glory to?
Philippians 2:10
That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; 11
And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
Note:

Recognizing and confessing Christ as Lord brings glory to God the Father. The Bible instructs us to worship the Father and the Son. It gives no instruction to worship any other being. This shows us that there are no other divine beings worthy of worship. When we worship Jesus as Lord, we are also giving glory to His Father.
21. Who else tries to receive worship?
Revelation 14:9
And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice,
If any man
worship
the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand,
The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation
; (See also Matt 4:8-9)
Note:
This text is speaking about the mark of the beast. At the end of time there is a warning about a false system of worship. The end time’s beast power demands worship that belongs to divinity alone.

God and His Son alone deserve worship. Jesus deserves worship because He was begotten of His Father. The beast power’s claim for worship is based upon lies. He has no direct lineage to God and therefore is not divine and should not be worshiped!
We should be alert to any deception that requires us to worship anything except true divinity.
The devil has attacked the church regarding the Bible verse of John 3:16.

Most do not realize that they do not really believe that God so loved the world that He gave His Son. Most Christians would openly tell you that they do indeed believe every word of John 3:16. But at the same time, they also believe other doctrines that deny this fact.
The main issue at hand is the belief in
three co-eternal beings

. This doctrine was not believed by the early church. It came into Christianity in 325 A.D. at the Council of Nicea. In Jude 3 we are admonished to earnestly contend for the faith ONCE DELIVERED TO THE SAINTS. So, let’s take a look at how this new heretical view has destroyed our belief in John 3:16.
Today’s false three-in-one God doctrine teaches us that God consists of
3 co-equal and co-eternal beings that make up one God
. If this is true, then both the Father and the Son would be
co-eternal;

therefore, they would both be the same age (eternal). If both are the same age, then one cannot be a father and the other a son. The false teaching that Jesus is eternal means that Jesus was never really begotten. Instead, it teaches that Jesus has always existed.
It also teaches that the word "begotten" does not really mean "begotten" and "son" does not really mean "a son". It teaches that the Bible uses these words as metaphors.
So, there you have it. The devil has slowly adjusted our beliefs to the point where we deny the most famous text in the Bible: John 3:16.

When confronted with these facts, most Christians exclaim, "It doesn't really matter.” But does it really matter? Yes, it is more important than we think. What has happened is that the devil has obscured the real Father and Son from our view. What has been obscured is the Bible's teaching that God so loved the world. John 3:16 is God's demonstration that He is a loving Father. This verse teaches that because of God's deep love, He has emptied heaven of its most precious gift, ” The Son of God.” The devil tells lies and says that "Son" does not really mean son and "begotten" does not really mean begotten.

What happens when our view of God's love is obscured? The problem runs deeper than we think. This false teaching could prevent us from developing a character like Christ’s. Man cannot love more than God loves. If we see that God only loves a little, we can only love a little. But if we see that God loves a lot, then we can love a lot. When we see that God loves us so much that He gave His only Son—it will enable us to love our enemies likewise. The Bible tells us that when we were yet His enemies (sinners), we were reconciled to God. (See Romans 5:10) If we cannot see God's love, we cannot love as He loves.

It is by beholding His love that we become changed, little by little, from glory to glory, into the same image, even by the Spirit of the Lord. (See 2 Corinthians 3:18) By obscuring our view of God’s love, the devil has prevented many from developing a Christ-like character of love.

Often the true love of God gets obscured, and cannot come clearly into focus. When the gospel is presented without showing God’s real begotten Son, or when God is presented as someone who tortures people for all eternity, the true deep love of a tender Father is obscured from our view. (See Lesson 8, “When we Die”)
But there is good news! By beholding God’s true love, our characters can become like His character, for we can then see Him as He is.

When we contemplate the love and humility of God we respond by giving Him praise. This praise is often demonstrated in heartfelt song, and this is exactly what praise and worship should look like: a heartfelt response to seeing the love of God.
1 John 3:2
Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see Him as He is.
